quiz.q: Where do you get the Object Store operations in Studio?
options: They are in the Core palette by default
From the HTTP connector's Advanced tab
quiz.explain: The Object Store isn't in the palette by default; add it through Add Modules.

quiz.q: Which two Object Store operations does the watermark use case need?
quiz.explain: Retrieve gets the last watermark; Store saves the new one under the same key.

quiz.q: On the very first run, no watermark has been stored yet. What makes the Retrieve still work?
quiz.explain: Retrieve returns the configured default value when the key doesn't exist yet.

quiz.q: What is the default of the Persistent checkbox in the Object Store config?
quiz.explain: Persistent is checked by default; unchecking it makes the store transient.

quiz.q: A watermark is stored at 10:00 with Entry TTL 1 hour. What happens at 11:00?
options: It expires, but is only removed when the expiration interval's background check runs
It moves to a persistent store
quiz.explain: Expiring doesn't remove the entry — the expiration interval's periodic cleanup deletes expired entries.

quiz.q: TTL is 1 hour and the expiration interval is 2 hours. What is the effect?
options: Expired entries may stay up to an extra hour before cleanup
quiz.explain: Created 10:00, expires 11:00, next check at 12:00 → it stays an extra hour. Keep the interval less than the TTL.

quiz.q: Which query selects only new employees using the watermark variable?
options: `select * from EMPLOYEES_INFO where emp_id > :emp_id` with `emp_id = vars.empWatermark`
quiz.explain: Only records newer than the stored watermark come back.

quiz.q: What value is stored after the records are created in Salesforce?
quiz.explain: Storing the highest ID under the same key overwrites the old watermark.

quiz.q: The first run in class retrieved 120 instead of the default 99. Why?
options: An earlier run had stored 120, and the persistent store kept it across the redeploy
quiz.explain: Persistent values survive stopping and redeploying the app.

quiz.q: A run finds no new records and fails: "You called the function 'max' with these arguments: 1: Null". What is the fix?
options: Wrap Create and Store in a Choice that runs only when records came back (`sizeOf(payload) > 0`), else log "no data"
quiz.explain: An empty payload makes `payload.emp_id` null, so `max(null)` fails; a Choice guards it.

quiz.q: What kind of column makes a good watermark?
options: Any text column such as name
A sequential, incremental column like an auto-increment ID or serial number
quiz.explain: The watermark column must be sequential and incremental; gaps are fine.

quiz.q: For checking only whether the payload is empty, which function is better?
quiz.explain: `sizeOf` works out the whole payload's size; `isEmpty` is better just to check emptiness.

cards.front: How do you implement watermarking in Mule?
cards.back: Scheduler → Object Store **Retrieve** (default value) → DB Select `where id > :lastId` → process → **Store** `max(payload.id)` under the same key. Use a persistent store.
Store, Retrieve, Retrieve All, Retrieve All Keys, Contains, Remove, Clear.
Saves a value under a key; storing under the same key overwrites the old value.
Gets the value for a key; returns the **default value** if the key doesn't exist yet.
`empWatermark` — the same as the key name, easier to remember.
Checked (persistent). Uncheck it for a transient store.
Limit on how many entries the store can hold.
**Time to live** — how long a value is valid (seconds, minutes, hours or days).
How often a background check runs to **delete** expired entries.
TTL = validity; the interval = how often expired entries are actually deleted. Keep the interval shorter than the TTL.
Persistent (default) keeps values across restarts and redeploys — needed for watermarks. Transient loses them — fine for a short-lived token.

cards.front: What breaks when there are no new records?
cards.back: `max(payload.emp_id)` gets null and fails ("expects Array"). Guard it with a Choice — `sizeOf(payload) > 0` (or `isEmpty`).

cards.front: What column makes a good watermark?
cards.back: A sequential, incremental one — an auto-increment ID or serial number. Gaps are fine.

cards.front: Why did the first run use 120 instead of the default 99?
cards.back: An earlier run had stored it, and the persistent store kept it across the redeploy.
"Around 30 days" — the instructor wasn't sure. A watermark must not expire.
`sizeOf` returns the size; `isEmpty` is better just to check whether the payload is empty.
Implement the access-token use case with a **transient** store (uncheck Persistent).
